acts.title: The Eunuch's Charge — Arsetes
acts.desc: Pilgrim Keeper's Quarter, Jerusalem. Arsetes — old, diminishing — holds a grey linen pouch pressed with a tigress paw. Inside: the Ethiopian queen's sealed letter to the Shrine of St. George, carried thirty years and never delivered. He cannot explain. He holds the pouch out. Insight DC 12: the transfer must happen without ceremony — asking questions would require him to say the things he cannot say.
acts.passText: The Fighter picks it up. Arsetes nods once. His hand stops shaking.
acts.failText: The Fighter reaches for it with a question. Arsetes pulls back. After a long silence he pushes it forward again without looking. The token is granted — but Arsetes does not nod. He turns his face to the wall.

acts.title: The Eunuch's Charge — Records Officer
acts.desc: Hospice gate road. A Crusade records officer has logged the pouch as an unclaimed Saracen dispatch. He wants it returned for military intelligence review. The pouch is a votive document — the Latin translation inside establishes Christian religious purpose; the seal is Ethiopian royal, not Saracen military. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: The officer notes it as 'votive document, released to authorized carrier, destination: shrine.' He initials it. The Fighter walks through the gate.
acts.failText: The officer keeps the pouch forty-eight hours while an interpreter is found. The Fighter waits, then argues again at DC 11. Delay: half a day.

acts.title: The Eunuch's Charge — Limestone Road
acts.desc: Limestone road toward SGA. Two armed servants of a relic-collecting Crusade knight are waiting. He has sent them to acquire the Ethiopian queen's sealed letter as a relic. The argument: a votive letter is not a relic — its content derives from being delivered, not from being possessed; intercepting it is stealing a payment. Persuasion DC 14; combat 2× AC 12 HP 14 if failed.
acts.passText: The servants stand aside.
acts.failText: Combat: two soldiers, AC 12, HP 14 each. After combat the pouch is intact — the servants were not authorized to damage it.

acts.title: The Eunuch's Charge — Shrine Gate
acts.desc: Shrine town outer gate. A new town-council regulation taxes sealed documents entering town to fund shrine roof repairs. A votive letter addressed to the shrine as a donation is not cargo in transit but cargo addressed here — taxing it on arrival taxes the donation fund. The gate-keeper is not persuadable; the council wrote 'sealed documents' with no exceptions. Athletics DC 13: a secondary entrance through a low wall in the eastern quarter, no toll, requires a controlled descent without dropping the old cloth.
acts.passText: The Fighter reaches the shrine precincts without engaging the tollgate.
acts.failText: The toll is paid. No delay; minor resource cost. But the Fighter arrives from the main entrance.

acts.title: The Eunuch's Charge — The Shrine
acts.desc: Shrine of St. George, donation office. Brother Matthias reads the Latin translation. He reads the date. He finds in his register an entry from thirty years past: projected donation from an Ethiopian royal family — marked 'awaited.' Insight DC 12: understand what he means when he says 'She was kept.'
acts.passText: The Fighter understands: the saint's contract was performed completely across thirty years of war. The letter was late but not refused. Brother Matthias draws a line through 'awaited' and writes the date. He places the letter in the sealed vault. He says: 'She was kept.'
acts.failText: Brother Matthias files the letter and notes the delay in the register. The delivery is complete. The debt is discharged.

acts.title: Sophronia's Witness — Olindo
acts.desc: Jerusalem inner quarter. Olindo gives the Fighter his deposition: he ran forward and falsely claimed Sophronia's crime, trying to take her death at the stake. The Saracen court record logs it as theft and conviction — not sacrifice and false confession. The record is being transferred to permanent archive status. A scribe is waiting. WIS DC 11: understand exactly what Olindo needs from the notarized deposition.
acts.passText: The scribe certifies without caveat. His stylus moves. Olindo signs. The deposition is sealed.
acts.failText: The scribe adds a caveat: 'deponent's account, accuracy disputed.' Not ideal, but the deposition is signed. Alexios will flag the caveat when he sees it.

acts.title: Sophronia's Witness — Expedited Closure
acts.desc: Jerusalem archive, outside the land registry. A Crusade administration official wants to file an expedited closure on the conviction record before the deposition can be entered — expedited closure makes permanent filing immediate. There is an exclusion clause in the archive regulations for records under active deposition challenge. Persuasion DC 13: cite the exclusion clause before he reaches the desk.
acts.passText: You cite the exclusion clause. He checks it. He finds it. He acknowledges the distinction and withdraws the expedited order.
acts.failText: He reaches the desk first. The expedited closure is filed. But the seal is not yet set — Alexios has a three-hour review window before the wax closes it.

acts.title: Sophronia's Witness — The Window
acts.desc: Archive registrar Alexios's office. You need the exact window before the conviction record is permanently sealed. WIS DC 11: understand Alexios's answer precisely — he gives the window in archival time, not clock time.
acts.passText: Alexios gives you the exact window: two hours. You note it. You leave.
acts.failText: You leave without confirming the time window and lose twenty minutes retracing. The return trip is tight.

acts.title: Sophronia's Witness — Sophronia's Signature
acts.desc: Sophronia is in the next room. She has read the deposition. She knows that signing it makes her lie — the false confession that saved the community — a matter of permanent record. WIS DC 12: understand what she means when she says 'Olindo knew what I was doing.'
acts.passText: She says: 'Olindo knew what I was doing.' She picks up the stylus. She signs carefully, her name in full. She hands it back without looking at it.
acts.failText: She takes the deposition and signs without speaking. She does not look at the Fighter afterward. She has decided something and is keeping it to herself.

acts.title: Sophronia's Witness — Registry
acts.desc: Alexios's desk, within the two-hour window. The dual-signed deposition versus the conviction record. WIS DC 11: understand what 'formal supplementation' means — it places both documents in the permanent record side by side rather than the conviction record alone.
acts.passText: Alexios enters it as formal supplementation: conviction record plus dual-signed deposition, notation that both exist and were submitted by named parties before the record was sealed. He stamps both. 'Both will be read,' he says.
acts.failText: Alexios enters it as commentary — 'sworn account appended by living parties.' The conviction record is not overridden, but the supplementing account is in the permanent record alongside it. Anyone consulting it finds both.

acts.title: Tancred's Grant — Land Session
acts.desc: Jerusalem land allocation session, one hour before close. Tancred's petition tablet: an olive-wood board with five boundary marks of a small valley northwest of the city wall — the valley where he killed Clorinda — and a chapel site request. On the reverse, scratched in haste: 'this is where she died.' Persuasion DC 12: ask the desk clerk to log the petition as received before the session ends.
acts.passText: The clerk logs the petition. The session closes with Tancred's valley on record.
acts.failText: The session closes. The clerk logs it in the first slot of the next session. One day's delay.

acts.title: Tancred's Grant — Competing Petition
acts.desc: A knight waiting outside has a competing orchard petition for the same valley. History DC 11: the valley is the site of a named combat in the Crusade's military record — that classification makes it unavailable for agricultural allocation.
acts.passText: Bernard receives this and withdraws.
acts.failText: Bernard contests the military record classification. A review of the battle log confirms it the next morning. He withdraws.

acts.title: Tancred's Grant — Byzantine Collector
acts.desc: Constantinople. A Byzantine collector wants the tablet as a relic — the reverse line ('this is where she died'). Insight DC 12: the line requires the five boundary marks to be meaningful; removed from its registry function it becomes grief-decoration without context. He needs a geographer's copy, not the original.
acts.passText: He commissions a geographer's copy instead. The original continues.
acts.failText: He makes a second offer. You decline. He commissions a copy through official channels and lets you pass.

acts.title: Tancred's Grant — Customs Authorization
acts.desc: Byzantine customs requires written authorization for carved objects leaving Constantinople. Athletics DC 12: collect the authorization, return, and reach the evening gate before closure — two trips through a busy customs district without damaging the olive-wood tablet.
acts.passText: You collect the authorization in time and pass through the gate before it closes.
acts.failText: You arrive at the gate with two minutes to spare. The gate guard is already reaching for the bar. You show the authorization through the gap.

acts.title: Tancred's Grant — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck reads both faces of the tablet. Investigation DC 11: confirm no existing category covers sites whose significance is simultaneous with the event that created them.
acts.passText: Sweelinck creates: Council Land Grants — Sites Marked by Irresolvable Personal History, First Entry. He files the tablet as a registry document and a location-record simultaneously.
acts.failText: Filed under Crusade land grants, Jerusalem district. The tablet is in the archive.

acts.title: Ismen's Notebooks — Scholar's Argument
acts.desc: Pilgrim's Quarter. Magister Aldo found Ismen's architectural notebook in his quarters after the sorcerer was killed — seventy pages documenting how the enchanted forest was built layer by layer. The destruction order on the cover classifies it as 'materials employed in black art, to be burned.' Aldo's argument: the notebook documents architectural method; it does not employ enchantment. History DC 11: the distinction holds under archive law.
acts.passText: You have the argument before anyone asks for it.
acts.failText: You carry the notebook without internalizing the distinction. You will need to make the argument under pressure in Act II without preparation.

acts.title: Ismen's Notebooks — Destruction Order
acts.desc: PKR quarter gate. A Crusade captain enforcing the destruction order stops the Fighter. The order reads 'materials employed in black art.' The notebook documents the architecture of enchantment; it does not employ enchantment. Persuasion DC 13: 'employed' requires active use; documentation is passive.
acts.passText: He reads the order again. He reads the cover notation. He accepts the distinction and lets you pass with a warning.
acts.failText: He detains the notebook for twenty-four hours pending council review. The Fighter waits.

acts.title: Ismen's Notebooks — Venetian Factor
acts.desc: Venice archive district. A Venetian factor wants to purchase the notebook for a Levantine collector with genuine scholarly interest. Insight DC 12: the scholarly interest deserves the correct answer — the archive provides access to researchers without transferring custody to a private collection where the destruction order's status remains unresolved.
acts.passText: He receives the distinction. He notes Weimar's access protocols and says his client will send a letter of inquiry. This is an acceptable outcome.
acts.failText: He makes a second, higher offer. You decline again. He follows you to the harbor.

acts.title: Ismen's Notebooks — Dominican Authorization
acts.desc: Venice harbor road. A Dominican friar carries a Papal letter authorizing him to collect 'materials related to black magic.' He is polite and believes he is performing a service. Deception DC 13: the notebook is an architectural record of method — not a spellbook or active instrument. His authorization cannot logically cover a technical manual without also covering every alchemical notebook in Venice.
acts.passText: He accepts the classification. He notes the Weimar destination in his record. He lets you pass.
acts.failText: He flags the notebook for forwarding to the Papal legate for assessment. A two-week delay while the legate's office in Avignon reads a letter.

acts.title: Ismen's Notebooks — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck reads the architectural diagrams. He reads the harmonic sequence tables. He looks at the destruction order on the cover and begins to remove the wax seal. Investigation DC 11: stop him — the order is the central evidence of the notebook's survival and belongs with the record.
acts.passText: Sweelinck stops. He sets down the wax tool. He files them together. His notation: 'Architectural Records of Supernatural Intervention — The Construction Behind the Illusion, First Entry. The destruction order on the cover will remain attached.'
acts.failText: Sweelinck removes the seal before you speak. The destruction order is filed separately. The notebook is separated from the evidence of its own survival.

acts.title: Erminia's Safe Passage — Shepherd Valley
acts.desc: Jerusalem inner quarter. Erminia hands the Fighter Godfrey's estate grant and says: 'He does not know what I look like without armor or wool.' Insight DC 11: the identity problem is not the document's — it is hers. The garrison commander has seen Clorinda's silver armor but not Erminia.
acts.passText: You understand before she finishes. 'Who saw you in the shepherd valley who knows your name?' She gives you two names.
acts.failText: You take the parchment without grasping the identity problem. You will face it unprepared.

acts.title: Erminia's Safe Passage — Silver Armor
acts.desc: Garrison commander's office. He has a report: Clorinda's silver armor was seen moving through the Christian camp at night. He suspects espionage. Persuasion DC 12: she borrowed the armor to heal Tancred, not gather intelligence; she was lost when the patrol chased her; she found the shepherds. Godfrey's grant was issued on the basis of the full account.
acts.passText: He accepts the sequence. He makes a note in the report and moves to the document assessment.
acts.failText: He forwards the armor question to a Crusade security assessment. The file is open pending review. Delay.

acts.title: Erminia's Safe Passage — Origin Challenge
acts.desc: Land registry desk. A records clerk: Erminia's father was a Saracen vassal ruler; estates held by Saracen rulers are subject to administrative review before any grant to Saracen-lineage heirs can be finalized. History DC 12: Godfrey's grant is not a succession instrument — it is a new-administration grant to a specific named person based on her current Christian ally status.
acts.passText: The clerk rereads the grant's legal basis. He accepts the distinction and processes the registration.
acts.failText: The clerk files a request for legal opinion. Two weeks.

acts.title: Erminia's Safe Passage — River Crossing
acts.desc: Road north from Jerusalem — a ford running high from spring snowmelt. The estate grant is parchment; Godfrey's seal is wax. The document cannot get wet. Athletics DC 11: knee-deep, fast current, loose gravel footing, document held above head.
acts.passText: You cross with the document dry. Godfrey's seal is sharp and unaffected.
acts.failText: You slip once. The document corner catches a splash. The parchment is damp but legible; the seal impression is slightly softened but intact.

acts.title: Erminia's Safe Passage — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck reads the grant. He reads the garrison commander's identity verification notation. He says: 'She was a shepherd for how long?' Religion DC 11: the grant references Erminia's father's tomb — under pilgrimage access provisions, tomb access is a separate legal category from property inheritance. Note this before he closes the file.
acts.passText: Sweelinck adds a notation covering both provisions. He writes: 'Identity Verification Records — The Person Who Has Been Someone Else and Returns, First Entry. The garrison commander's identity confirmation is the document's primary provenance chain.' He files.
acts.failText: The tomb access provision is filed under general estate rights. The distinction is lost.

acts.title: Armida's Conversion — Before She Leaves
acts.desc: Damascus. Armida stands at the window of the house she will not see again. The declaration is on the table — she has already written it. Her stylus is in her hand and she is not moving. Persuasion DC 13: give her the specific distinction — signing opens the process of claiming her Damascus properties under Christian protection, not surrendering them.
acts.passText: She hears the distinction. She picks up the stylus. She signs both copies in full, titles included.
acts.failText: She signs without being given the distinction. She files the declaration. She will ask about the properties later and the question will be harder to answer.

acts.title: Armida's Conversion — Damascus Gate
acts.desc: Damascus city gate. A civil official has a contested-property flag on outbound documents naming those estates — his interpretation is that a conversion declaration affecting property rights is a property document. Insight DC 12: a personal religious status declaration is not a property document; it precedes property decisions and is independent of them.
acts.passText: He reads the argument. He lifts the flag for status instruments. You pass with the declaration.
acts.failText: He holds the declaration for forty-eight hours while the distinction is reviewed. You wait.

acts.title: Armida's Conversion — Byzantine Ecclesiastical
acts.desc: Constantinople Byzantine ecclesiastical administration. The official wants a Bishop's countersignature before ratifying Christian protection for a converted sorceress. Persuasion DC 12: Rinaldo's countersignature under field authority is sufficient — the same authority as all other legal instruments of the campaign; requiring episcopal co-signature retroactively would invalidate them all.
acts.passText: He accepts the Crusade administration's authority. He ratifies the declaration and adds his notation: 'valid under field authority.'
acts.failText: He writes a letter requesting episcopal review. The declaration is valid but with a conditional notation. Delay.

acts.title: Armida's Conversion — Papal Agent
acts.desc: Road junction north of Constantinople. A Dominican agent on horseback with Papal instructions to divert the declaration to Rome as a diplomatic precedent. Deception DC 13: it is a private status document — one woman's legal status, not an international precedent. Rome may make a formal archival request if they want a copy.
acts.passText: He accepts the classification. He notes his instructions will require Rome to make a formal archival request. He lets you pass.
acts.failText: He forwards a copy of his instructions to the Weimar archive as a challenge to the filing. The declaration arrives encumbered.

acts.title: Armida's Conversion — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck reads both copies. He looks at the damascene rose impression in the wax — she designed her own seal. He reads the Damascus property attachment. Investigation DC 11: standard conversion categories don't fit; she came as a weapon and declared as herself — the archive needs the category that holds both before and after.
acts.passText: Sweelinck creates: 'Conversion Records — The Former Enemy's Declaration Made Under Her Own Authority, First Entry. She came to the Crusade camp as a weapon and left it as herself; the damascene rose in the wax is her device; what she declared she declared without being required to.'
acts.failText: He files it under standard conversion records. The 'formerly of Damascus, ward of Hidraoth' is absorbed into a category that doesn't hold what it says.

acts.title: The Godfrey Dispatch — Wounded Courier
acts.desc: Pilgrim hospice back room. The courier has a crossbow bolt wound and beginning fever. He cannot give you the ship departure time, recipient name, or routing instructions. He holds an oiled leather cylinder — Godfrey's eagle seal — and pushes it toward the Fighter. Insight DC 11: the commission is to carry the letter to Rome before the sailing window closes, not to understand it.
acts.passText: You take the cylinder. He relaxes. You find the ship by asking the harbor master who is holding a Crusade dispatch commission.
acts.failText: You ask three questions he cannot answer. He loses consciousness before the transfer completes. You take the cylinder anyway, but you don't know the ship.

acts.title: The Godfrey Dispatch — Raymond's Agent
acts.desc: PKR harbor road. Raymond of Toulouse's agent is waiting. He wants to delay you thirty minutes with a false countersignature requirement — long enough for Raymond's own dispatch to be loaded first. Persuasion DC 12: Godfrey's dispatches carry command authority by unanimous election; the blank receipt is a delay mechanism, not a procedural requirement.
acts.passText: He accepts the argument. He watches you go. He does not follow.
acts.failText: He delays you fifteen minutes. The sailing window is tighter. You make the harbor at a run.

acts.title: The Godfrey Dispatch — Vatican Archive
acts.desc: Vatican archive intake, Rome. The records official wants to file under 'Crusade Administration — General Dispatches' — an uncatalogued section effectively burying it. History DC 12: a commander's dispatch describing the conclusion of a Papal-sanctioned campaign is a primary command document with its own canon law category.
acts.passText: He rereads the canon law category table. He accepts the classification. He files it as a primary commander's dispatch.
acts.failText: He files it under Administration. Godfrey's version is buried. Raymond's version, filed three hours earlier as a primary record, is the accessible account.

acts.title: The Godfrey Dispatch — Alpine Bridge
acts.desc: Alpine pass north of Rome. A single bridge over the runoff channel — twelve feet, wet planks, slick rope rail, fast channel eight feet below. The oiled leather cylinder must not be submerged. Athletics DC 13: cross with the cylinder held inside your cloak, one hand on the rope rail, weight distributed carefully.
acts.passText: You cross without incident. The cylinder is dry. You descend the northern slope in good time.
acts.failText: Your foot slips at the midpoint. You catch the rope rail. The cylinder stays inside your cloak — dry, but you spent thirty seconds with one hand on the rope and your heart going.

acts.title: The Godfrey Dispatch — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck reads the dispatch. He reads the Crusade seal on both ends. He notices a hairline crack across the eagle's wing on the right-side seal. 'This crack — is it new?' Perception DC 11: the crack is from the Alpine crossing; the seal was intact in Jerusalem; the letter was not opened.
acts.passText: You tell him: the crack is from the Alpine crossing. The seal was intact in Jerusalem. He writes the provenance note. He creates: 'Commander's Dispatches — The Account That Names Its Own Differences From the Competing Version, First Entry.' He files. questComplete.
acts.failText: You cannot say definitively when the crack occurred. Sweelinck notes it as 'condition uncertain at receipt' — a provenance question that will follow the document.
